I read Katz-Sarnak sections11.4.1-11.4.9, including the full proof and the image of printed p.334 (PDF page343), from the matching-hash author PDF. Theorem11.4.9 assumes d>=3, n>=1 and (n,d)!=(2,3), and states the Sp/O conclusion on every geometric fibre over Z[1/ell]. Neither the theorem nor the standing definitions require odd residue characteristic. Its proof treats p!=ell via a sufficiently general Lefschetz pencil and excludes finite even-dimensional monodromy using n(d-2)>=4; the image confirms the non-strict inequality, including its equality cases. Remove the added p-odd restriction from item34, preserve the cubic-surface exception and distinguish hypersurface dimension n=r-1 from ambient dimension r. The circle-method application still has its own p>k assumption. This verifies the source statement and proof as written, not all its cited subsidiary results.

The two prime-existence inputs are missing as separate interfaces. Credit the Dirichlet and reciprocity statements as library inputs, then plan two proved adapters: for fixed odd p>k choose prime ell congruent to -1 mod p, giving order2; for fixed odd ell choose a nonzero nonsquare a mod ell and primes p congruent to1 mod4 and a mod ell, using CRT, Dirichlet and reciprocity. For ell=2 use primes p congruent to5 mod8 and the supplementary law. Choose bounds excluding p=ell and all bad characteristics. A nonsquare has even multiplicative order because F_p^x is cyclic. Do not certify the composite adapters as already in Mathlib. Any source-issue entry should describe an implicit prime-choice justification and complete its section18 correction search before calling it new; it is not a counterexample to the geometric corollary.
